title: What Can We Learn About Happiness From the People Who Study It? - Nautilus
gist: Thirteen pioneers of happiness research, with a collective 600 years of experience, reflected on the field's half century in the Journal of Happiness Studies. The author stresses it was a reflective summary rather than a rigorous empirical study.

insights.claim: Happiness research emerged as a field in the 1970s, coalescing from a nebulous constellation of other disciplines, whereas science has asked how to live longer for centuries.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Well-being science is a relatively young field compared with longevity research, implying its policy and commercial applications are still maturing.
insights.quote: The field of happiness research first emerged in the 1970s, coalescing from a nebulous constellation of other disciplines.

insights.claim: Thirteen happiness researchers with a collective 600 years of experience gathered to reflect on the past half century of happiness research and published the results in the Journal of Happiness Studies.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Field-level retrospectives can shape which well-being metrics policymakers adopt.
insights.quote: Altogether, 13 happiness researchers (and some family members) with a collective 600 years of experience contributed to the conversation.

insights.claim: The happiness pioneers' published reflection was not a rigorous empirical investigation but a summary of a gathering of researchers, some of whom applied lessons from their work to their own lives.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Treat conclusions from expert-reflection pieces as opinion rather than evidence when assessing well-being claims.
insights.quote: Importantly, this wasn’t a rigorous empirical investigation.
